takeaway: IMN Thursday keeps Pacífico Norte in rainy-season mode: morning little–partly cloudy, afternoon showers with storms over the center and south of the region, and a possible night shower near the Gulf of Nicoya (Nicoya ~32°C; Liberia ~36°C). Hurricane Polo remains a major hurricane well offshore southwestern Mexico, Hurricane Odalys stays far west in the open EPAC, and the Tehuantepec genesis area is still high (~80% in 7 days) tracking parallel to southern Mexico — no cyclone near Costa Rica. Gyre/temporales watch stays elevated, not established: ensemble means keep Pacific SW low-level moisture into Nicoya through the weekend into early next week, without a closed land gyre.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Thu–Sat)
periods.pattern: Today (IMN Pacífico Norte, valid Thu 24 Sep): morning little–partly cloudy; afternoon partly cloudy with showers and storms over the center and south; evening little–partly cloudy with a possible localized shower near the Gulf of Nicoya. General commentary: typical rainy-season humidity/instability — afternoon storms Valle Central, Pacífico Sur, Pac Norte center/north, and Pac Central mountains; night rains/aguaceros along Pacific coasts. Nicoya max ~32.1°C / min ~23.3°C (Liberia ~36.0°C). Weekly: maritime Pacific rains more evident Mon–Wed mornings; Wed onward rains/aguaceros with storm in Pac Central/Sur and Pac Norte mountains / Valle Central; OT#46 estimated this weekend with little country signal. GFS 06Z / GEFS mean 06Z / EPS mean 00Z / AIFS-ENS 00Z 24-h maps keep Nicoya mostly light–moderate (~0.1–0.75 in / 24 h) through ~Sat morning. GEFS mean f024 and EPS mean f024 show light SW–W 850 onshore over Nicoya with flanking EPAC lows (EPS ~985 hPa class feature near southern Mexico/Guatemala waters; GEFS ~1001 hPa class west of CR) — moist monsoon trough / ITCZ, not a closed land gyre. Papagayo variable <5–light, seas ~3–6 ft (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113).
periods.implications: Mornings still the better outdoor window; plan around afternoon storms (IMN: Pac Norte center/south) and a possible night shower near the Gulf of Nicoya. Inland Guanacaste stays very hot (Liberia mid–upper 30s).
periods.confidence: High for no nearby TC and continued ITCZ shower/storm chances (IMN + NHC). Moderate on exact Nosara timing/amounts (IMN afternoon storms vs light–moderate ensemble means).

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sun–Wed)
periods.pattern: Sun (~27 Sep): GEFS mean 06Z epac f072 keeps W–SW 850 over Nicoya with ~1010 hPa EPAC L south of Guatemala/El Salvador and a deeper ~1002 hPa L farther west; EPS mean 00Z f072 shows a deeper ~993 hPa EPAC L off southern Mexico with light W–SW 850 over Nicoya; AIFS-ENS 00Z f072 similar (~992 hPa L south of Mexico, stronger SW 850). GFS deterministic 06Z epac f072 shows a deep TC-type center well west (~18°N/114°W class) plus a weaker ~1011 hPa L south of Guatemala — treat the deep feature as Mexico-parallel TC environment (Polo / next genesis), not a Costa Rica gyre. 24-h means: GEFS Nicoya ~0.3–0.75 in; EPS and AIFS-ENS lighter ~0.05–0.3 in over Nicoya with heavier moisture remaining offshore. By ~Tue 29 (f120), GEFS mean still shows SW–S 850 over Nicoya with precip ~0.1–0.4 in; EPS f120 also light–moderate ~0.1–0.4 in with weak W–SW 850 and no closed land gyre. NHC OFFPZ8 synopsis: moderate-or-weaker winds through the weekend with mainly moderate seas (locally rough western Guatemala early Thu only). Not locked as a multi-day temporal or closed Central American gyre.
periods.implications: Keep late-day plans flexible Sun–Tue if SW moisture holds; treat deeper EPS/AIFS EPAC lows as Mexico-parallel moisture signal, not a guaranteed temporales. Marine: Papagayo mostly light/variable with seas ~3–6 ft (NHC).
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued shower chances and persistent SW-moisture signal; low–moderate for sustained temporales or a closed Central American gyre (ensemble means lack a closed land gyre; Nicoya precip stays mostly light–moderate).

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: IMN sub-seasonal (21 Sep–18 Oct) still keeps Pacífico Norte below normal (weekly Pac Norte roughly 5–90 mm for 21–27 Sep and again 28 Sep–4 Oct) with stronger-than-usual trades limiting Pacific-side rain in the official narrative. CPC GTH text updated 22 Sep (valid 30 Sep–13 Oct): El Niño background; week-2/3 EPAC genesis areas lean Mexico / open EPAC, not CR; no CR-focused extreme rainfall call in the discussion excerpt. GEFS mean f168 (~1 Oct) still shows light SW 850 over Nicoya and light–moderate precip (~0.4–0.75 in / 24 h) without a local extreme bullseye or closed land gyre; EPS f168 is lighter (~0.15–0.4 in) with nearby highs and only weak SW. Heavy EPAC precip stays offshore Mexico. Single deterministic frames can still show a wetter day — treat as scenario only.
periods.implications: No official signal for a prolonged flood-season spike on the Nicoya Pacific side; short heavy cells remain possible.
periods.confidence: Moderate for below-normal / no major local TC theme; low for day-by-day rain.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Roughly weekend into early next week (~Sat–Tue 26–29 Sep) while flanking EPAC lows and Pacific SW low-level flow persist; GEFS mean still keeps Nicoya onshore SW through f120–f168 rather than a clean trade return
gyreWatch.supporting: GEFS mean 06Z f024–f168 shows SW–W 850 over Nicoya (epac panels clearest) with EPAC Ls ~1001–1010 hPa class; EPS mean 00Z f024–f120 and AIFS-ENS 00Z f072 keep SW onshore fetch and deeper EPAC lows (~985–993 hPa class, southern Mexico parallel). Short-term IMN ITCZ / Pac Norte afternoon storms + Gulf of Nicoya night-shower chance support a moist Pacific start. Versus midweek, SW-moisture window still extends through early next week on ensemble means.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Ensemble means do not show a closed gyre centered over Central America — pattern is flanking EPAC lows / monsoon trough plus SW moisture. GFS det deep EPAC lows are TC-type features near Mexico (Polo / next Tehuantepec system), not a CR gyre. Ensemble-mean Nicoya precip stays mostly light–moderate; EPS/AIFS f072 are actually lighter over Nicoya than GEFS. NHC has no disturbance near Costa Rica (Hurricane Polo and Hurricane Odalys well west/NW; Tehuantepec genesis 80% in 7 days tracks parallel to southern/southwestern Mexico). IMN sub-seasonal still favors Pacific rainfall deficit. Ensemble means only — no member-count probabilities.

whatChanged: New Thursday IMN Pac Norte: afternoon storms focused on center/south of the region; night language is a possible localized shower near the Gulf of Nicoya (vs Wed’s broader coastal-night rains). Wed evening IMN aviso (5:40 p.m.) confirmed afternoon storms with 6-hour totals including Liberia 52 mm — no new Thursday aviso listed yet at collection time. Polo still a major hurricane (~140 kt / 923 mb at 0900 UTC Thu) farther northwest offshore SW Mexico; Odalys remains a hurricane well west; Tehuantepec genesis still ~80% in 7 days. NHC OFFPZ8 eased: moderate-or-weaker winds through the weekend (yesterday’s fresher El Salvador/Guatemala Thu–early Sat bump is gone; only locally rough western Guatemala early today). Model theme similar to Wed: SW moisture persists into f120–f168, but EPS/AIFS Nicoya precip means at f072 look lighter than yesterday’s wetter EPS frames — still light–moderate overall, no closed land gyre.
practical: Best apparent outdoor windows: mornings Thu–Sat before the convective peak, noting IMN afternoon storms on Pac Norte center/south. Worth planning around: possible night shower near the Gulf of Nicoya, very warm inland heat (Liberia ~36°C; Nicoya ~32°C), and Papagayo light/variable with seas ~3–6 ft (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113). Watch Sat–Tue if SW moisture and the Tehuantepec/Mexico-parallel lows verify wetter than GEFS. Latest IMN aviso is Wed 23 Sep 5:40 p.m. (afternoon/evening storms) — no new Thursday aviso listed yet.
